question: public measured datasets that constrain the Q127 myonuclei accretion/retention model in inputs/

sources.title: Muscle fiber size, myonuclear domain, and fat mass phenotypes in pre-migratory snow buntings
sources.authors: Vezina F, O’Connor R, Le Pogam A, De Jesus A, Love O, Jimenez A
sources.format: XLSX (Office Open XML), 1 sheet, 15 rows x 14 columns
sources.n_subjects: 15 birds (Plectrophenax nivalis), 15 data rows, 1 row per bird per experiment day
measured_observables: quantity labelled "Myonuclear domain" (unit absent from the file)
sources.constraint_note: Per-fibre nuclei counts and per-fibre diameter are exactly the two quantities the model takes from Cumming et al. 2024 (M0, A0), here in a non-human species. The derived cross-sectional area pi/4*d^2 spans 628-1134 um^2 over the 15 birds; the model A0 = 4029 um^2 is equivalent to a diameter of 71.6 um, i.e. outside the measured range of this dataset. The "Myonuclear domain" column is NOT usable: it carries no unit and fails an internal consistency check (see results.json load report).

sources.title: Single-cell chromatin accessibility profiling reveals a self-renewing muscle satellite cell state - raw quantification tables
sources.authors: Okafor A, Diao Y, Lin X, Situ C, Wei X, Wu Z
sources.size: record total 1404592099 bytes across 16 files; the file used here is 12213 bytes
sources.format: XLSX, 1 sheet "Raw Counts", 38 rows x 26 columns; 13 WT and 13 Smad4-KO columns, 3-4 replicate columns per time point
sources.n_subjects: unit of replication is the fibre (38 fibres per column); the file contains no animal or limb identifier, so n animals is UNKNOWN from the sample
sources.species: Mus musculus (mouse), injury-induced regeneration, not exercise training
measured_observables: Pax7+ cell number on the fibre at 0, 24, 48 and 72 h, WT and Smad4-KO
sources.constraint_note: This is the only public per-fibre count of muscle precursor cells over time found in this run. It is the direct observable behind the model state S ("activated precursors/fibre") and therefore behind S0 = 0.1, a_base = 0.001 and k_cycle = 0.05, all three of which the frozen table marks as assumption. The 0 -> 72 h rise is a precursor-recruitment rate; it is not a fusion rate and not a myonuclear count.

sources.title: Ultrasound-derived changes in thickness of human ankle plantar flexor muscles during walking and running
sources.size: record total 605360 bytes across 4 files; MG_thickness.xlsx 204843 bytes, ReadMe.txt 568 bytes
sources.format: XLSX, 7 sheets (one per locomotion condition: walk 0.7/1.4/2.0, run 2.0/3.0/4.0/5.0), each 99 x 20 float64; plus a plain-text ReadMe
sources.n_subjects: 9 human participants (per the record ReadMe: "the mean change in thickness measured from nine participants")
measured_observables: mean change in muscle thickness (mm) vs gait-cycle phase, at 20 sites along each muscle, in 7 locomotion conditions
sources.constraint_note: The only human in-vivo time series in this inventory with a fully documented unit and coordinate frame. It bounds the RATE SCALE of in-vivo dimensional change: the largest absolute mean thickness change over one gait cycle is 3.698658 mm (peak-to-peak up to 4.49491 mm), i.e. millimetre-scale dimensional change within a single stride of about one second. It does NOT bound k_turn or k_inc numerically: the file reports a change in mm, not an absolute thickness, so no fractional rate per day can be formed. Recorded as a scale check, not a parameter bound.
sources.source_of_metadata: Zenodo REST API record 3976940 + the record ReadMe.txt

sources.title: Supplementary tables for Lavin KM et al. - module characteristics from human skeletal muscle biopsies
sources.size: record total 504083 bytes across 7 files; TableS1.xlsx 10977 bytes
sources.format: XLSX, 1 sheet, 46 rows x 3 columns after reading the 1-row caption header; 45 WGCNA modules
sources.n_subjects: not resolvable from the downloaded file - human skeletal-muscle-biopsy cohort upstream, but TableS1 is a module summary with no subject identifier
measured_observables: WGCNA module size (n unique transcripts) and module membership (kME) from human muscle biopsies; the parent study also measured % type I fibres and mean type I myofibre group size

sources.title: Preserved single muscle fiber specific force in facioscapulohumeral muscular dystrophy
sources.authors: Lassche S, Voermans NC, van der Pijl R, van den Berg M, Heerschap A, van Hees H
sources.format: DOCX (Office Open XML) containing supplementary tables; not parsed in this run
sources.n_subjects: 26 human subjects: 14 genetically confirmed FSHD patients and 12 healthy controls; 50 muscle biopsies (26 vastus lateralis, 24 tibialis anterior); 547 single fibres measured
measured_observables: single-fibre specific force, titin content, PEVK phosphorylation, per fibre
sources.constraint_note: A human per-fibre cohort with force measured per isolated fibre. The model has no force state, so the usable constraint is indirect: specific force per fibre relates the contractile pool P to area A and therefore tests the r_nuc / k_inc scaling. Not downloaded: the file is a .docx of tables, i.e. not machine-readable without OCR, and the brief asks for a demonstrated load, which four XLSX samples already provide.

sources.title: Scaling relationships between human leg muscle architectural properties and body size
sources.authors: Son J, Ward SR, Lieber RL
sources.license: NOT STATED for redistribution. The PMC record shows "(c) 2024. Published by The Company of Biologists Ltd" and "Deposited in PMC for immediate release"; no Creative Commons licence is declared on the article. Data availability statement: "All relevant data can be found within the article and its supplementary information."
sources.size: article + supplementary jexbio-227-246567-s1.pdf, 1.8 MB (per the PMC file listing)
sources.format: journal article tables + one supplementary PDF; no machine-readable table file is provided
sources.n_subjects: 34 human cadaveric lower extremities (18 F, 16 M, 36-103 y), 896 individual muscles across 28 muscles, 3 mapped regions per muscle
measured_observables: raw fibre length Lf (cm, digital caliper, 0.01 mm), normalised fibre length Lf = Lf\*(Ls,opt/Ls), bundle sarcomere length Ls (laser diffraction, Ls,opt = 2.7 um), PCSA (cm2), muscle mass (g)
sources.constraint_note: The largest human fibre-length dataset found in this run and the only human measurement of the model assumption fiber_length = 10000 um. The article reports CV of Lf across muscles of 19.9 +/- 5.7 % and states that fibre length does not scale with body mass. Half credit under prereg C1: the licence does not permit redistribution and the values sit in a PDF, so this is measured but not machine-readable and not redistributable.

sources.title: The Human Protein Atlas - skeletal muscle, single-cell and tissue data
sources.authors: Uhlen M et al. (Human Proteome Project)
sources.license: CC BY 4.0 for all copyrightable parts of the database (stated verbatim on the licence page). Third-party sources inside the atlas carry their own terms; the licence page lists GTEx and Ensembl as "User terms".
sources.size: per-gene TSV and JSON downloads, kilobytes each; the full release is a multi-GB archive. Not downloaded in this run.
sources.format: TSV / JSON per gene and per cell type
sources.n_subjects: human tissue and single-cell cohorts; the licence page cites Karlsson M et al., Sci Adv 2021, "A single-cell type transcriptomics map of human tissues" as the source of the single-cell atlas
measured_observables: skeletal-muscle cell-type clusters, including the clusters named Myonuclei, Myosatellite cells and Skeletal myofibers (cluster names read off the atlas cell-type facet), and per-cell-type expression of PAX7, MYOD1, MYF5, MYH1, MYH2
sources.constraint_note: The atlas classifies human skeletal-muscle nuclei into Myonuclei and Myosatellite cells, which is the human counterpart of the model split between the counted nuclei M and the precursor pool S. It bounds the precursor/myonuclei ratio and the fibre-type mixture. Indirect: the counted object is a transcriptomic nucleus, not a nucleus inside a fibre, so by falsifier F2 it constrains M0 only as an upper bound and is flagged as such.
sources.source_of_metadata: https://www.proteinatlas.org/about/licence (licence text and third-party table) and the cell-type facet list on the licence page

sources.title: GTEx Project - open-access gene and single-nucleus expression for Muscle - Skeletal
sources.license: GTEx Portal data licence, portal "License" page. The download page states that only open-access data files are available there, and that raw sequence data and full donor metadata are protected-access via dbGaP.

sources.constraint_note: Bulk skeletal-muscle RNA-seq gives the MYH1/MYH2 (type II) versus MYH7 (type I) transcript mixture and therefore the fraction of fibres to which a type-II M0 applies, and gives a large human cohort size for the baseline state. It cannot count nuclei per fibre. Marked half credit and the donor count is the only number verified here.

rejected.title: Cumming KT et al. 2024, "Muscle memory in humans: evidence for myonuclear permanence and long-term transcriptional regulation after strength training", J Physiol 602(17):4171-4193
rejected.reason: REJECTED as a public data source. This is the study the model takes M0 = 2.4 and A0 = 4029 from, and it is open access as an article, but no public machine-readable per-fibre dataset was found: the values are means in the Results text and figures. The Wiley full-text endpoint also returned HTTP 403 to this run. Consequence, applied per falsifier F1: the human values of M0 and A0 are downgraded to literature_only, and the entire R_excess reference (0.8888889) inherits that status.
rejected.type: literature with no redistributable raw data

rejected.title: In situ spatial transcriptomic analysis of human skeletal muscle using the Xenium platform
rejected.reason: REJECTED: the record page states "The record is publicly accessible, but files are restricted. Log in to check if you have access." Total data volume 671.0 GB, 754 views, 357 downloads, files restricted. A restricted record is not a public measured dataset under the brief. It is otherwise the most on-topic human spatial muscle dataset found (vastus lateralis, 2 individuals, 377 genes, serial sections stained for MyHC type 1 and MyHC 2a/2x).
